approval.approval_note: Approved for directional synthetic testing under the named proxy boundary.

claim_boundary: Public proxy frame only. employed-person-proxy: Employer-reported employed persons, excluding self-employed people.; employer-establishment-proxy: Employer establishments in published CBP rows.; employer-firm-proxy: Employer firms in published SUSB rows. These proxies do not represent the full commercial target audience.

limitations: The ACS/PUMS self-employed joint is unavailable.
BLS occupation cells are modeled employer-reported proxies and exclude self-employed people.

evidence_gaps.gap: The ACS/PUMS self-employed employment-status by geography joint is unavailable.
evidence_gaps.impact_on_panel: The person proxy cannot support Tier 2 composition.
evidence_gaps.mitigation: Downgrade to Tier 1 and retain the missing joint explicitly.

evidence_sources.limits: Persons, firms, and establishments remain separate; self-employed people are missing from the person proxy.
evidence_sources.source_label: Pinned BLS OEWS May 2025, Census SUSB 2022, and Census CBP 2023 extracts

creative_implications: Use the panel directionally and retain the explicit proxy boundary.
findings.inference_boundary: The fixture supports only the named public proxies and cannot represent the full commercial target.
findings.statement: The named public sources support separate person, firm, and establishment proxy universes, not one universal audience denominator.

privacy_confirmation.note: Only pinned public aggregate observations are included.

research_questions: Which public proxy boundaries can support directional creative testing?

segment_hypotheses.name: Marketing-leader public proxy
segment_hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_ad_testing: It provides a bounded directional audience profile without claiming full-market prevalence.

target_audience.audience: U.S. marketing and advertising decision-makers represented by the named public proxies
exclusions: Self-employed people are outside the employer-reported person proxy
